# NOTES: TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: *Pride and His Prisoners* (A. L. O. E.; Gutenberg 60149)

### Ch I, The Haunted Dwelling
- Spring Sabbath, Somersetshire. Nettleby Tower on a hill: Norman robber-hold, dry moat, rusted portcullis, Commonwealth siege bullet marks.
- Owner Mr. Auger got it by lawsuit that ruined the rightful heir. Last Mr. Bardon (Hugh) disinherited his only son Timon for marrying a farmer's daughter, over 30 years ago.
- Old woman guides tourists. Tower "haunted" by spirits of Pride and Intemperance.
- Dialogue on battlements: Intemperance: "I intoxicated his brain." Pride: "I intoxicated his spirit." Pride names three fermentations: vinous (high spirit), acid (sour brooding), last stage (hating and hated).
- Pride can't enter church ground, but enters worshippers and pulpit. Footnote: pastor's "devil told me the same thing" quip.
- Intemperance praises Ida Aumerle, pastor's daughter, "snowdrop." Pride: "Even the snowdrop has its roots in the earth."

### Ch II, Resisted, Yet Returning
- Ida Aumerle, age 12, lost mother; sister Mabel several years younger; tender father.
- Ida's vanity over mirror and dress. Conversion at night reading Bible: "birthday of a soul."
- Ida, age 18, at uncle Augustine Aumerle's home, Aspendale. Suitor Reginald, Earl of Dashleigh (Augustine's college friend). Ida refuses him. Dashleigh then proposes to cousin Annabella.
- Father remarries Miss Lambert, now Mrs. Aumerle (practical, sensible, the stepmother). Ida "dethroned"; Pride stirs friction.
- Pride's name in Ida's case: "sensitiveness."

### Ch III, Snares
- Mrs. Aumerle rejects Ida's three-voice anthem. Ida gives up music charge.
- Pastor Lawrence Aumerle, vicar of Ayrley, prosperous and complacent until wife's sickness and death humbled him.
- Augustine Aumerle: handsome, brilliant, Cambridge honours, intellectual pride, sceptic in progress ("German philosophy").
- Timon Bardon, long white hair, seen near tower.
- Narrator's preface: reader should check whether own soul is "a prisoner of Pride."

### Ch IV, A Glance into the Cottage
- Mill Cottage (Cecilia calls it "Milton Cottage"; Dr. Bardon insists "Mill"). Stone cottage, two storeys, iron knocker.
- Cecilia Bardon: sallow, light hair, grey eyes, 30–40 (age unknown). Dress and fashion are her pride. Fawn kid boots win over curtain and school subscription.
- Dr. Timon Bardon: surgeon, poor practice, leonine, dark flashing eyes, long white hair, downturned mouth. Says "No!" sharply. Favourite axiom: "It's the fool that gets on in the world."
- Pink paper wedding cards of Annabella (married "one year and ten months").
- Ida and Mabel bring crimson curtain. Bardon ungracious. Ida invites on Annabella's behalf to Dashleigh Hall. Bardon gives hyacinths to the girls.

### Ch V, Both Sides
- Mabel: "porcelain vs crockery"; Bardon's mental glass (magnifier for self, diminisher for others).
- Mrs. Aumerle scolds girls for crossing fields after sunset. Mabel angry; Ida calm.
- Ida plans farm-lads class on Saturday; mothers' meeting conflict. Mrs. Aumerle: Ida "teaching and preaching" unbecoming. Mrs. Aumerle will take lads herself, Ida gets mothers' class.
- Mrs. Aumerle quotes James 4:6 ("God resisteth the proud").

### Ch VI, The Visit to the Hall
- Dr. refuses Pelton clarence (6 miles); hires farmer's donkey-chaise. Cecilia's silk flounced dress. Bonnet touched up.
- Dashleigh lodge-keeper Mills admits them. Hall: "mere gingerbread" (Bardon).
- Annabella: small, Titania-like, irregular profile, dark vivacious eyes, romance manuscript, ink stain on finger.
- Annabella charms Bardon: garden, Venice Sumach slip. Cecilia's boots soiled by gravel.

### Ch VII, A Misadventure
- Annabella background: orphan, grandmother's pet. Pen name "Egeria." Earl offered hand after pique. Marriage sours; Pride whispers to each.
- Earl's Swiss mountain fear. Earl falls off horse when donkey brays. Earl orders "that brute" removed; Duke of Montleroy invited to luncheon; covers laid for four.
- Earl sends for wife. Annabella delays. Cecilia: "Yes" drawn out; Bardon: "No!"
- Earl overheard from library: "Can't you manage some way of getting rid of these miserable Bardons?"
- Bardon's thundering speech ("gilded puppet of society"). Leaves. Annabella weeps.

### Ch VIII, A Brother's Effort
- Augustine's remark at dinner about Bible. Lawrence confronts him in study.
- Argument: Reason as handmaid; mysteries; Psalm 131 read; "natural man receiveth not"; electricity and memory analogies.
- Augustine: sin "cant." Lawrence: "You do not know your own weakness and sin."
- Augustine storms out. Lawrence prays on knees.

### Ch IX, Disappointment
- Annabella revising proofs of "The Fairy Lake," violet and gold. Earl forbids publication except private circulation. Annabella: "Tyrant!" (Pride whispers).
- Annabella writes "The Precipice and the Peer" satirising earl's Swiss fear, with boa.

### Ch X, On the Watch
- April arbour. Mabel: Uncle Augustine says Ida "too good."
- Ida's "ladder" of works broken; "golden cord" of faith; prayer "dearest idol." Mabel's head on sister's bosom. Pride baffled.

### Ch XI, The Quarrel
- Earl & Annabella cool. Earl mentions Augustine invited them to balloon ascent at Aspendale (Verdon's balloon *Eaglet*).
- Annabella: "Throw etiquette to the dogs." Earl seeks *Magazine*, finds manuscript in drawer, reads "The Precipice and the Peer," tears it, tramples it.
- Earl: "Leave the room, insolent girl!" Duke of Montleroy witnesses.
- Annabella: "I shall sleep at the vicarage tonight." Maid Bates; coachman Mullins. Servants gossip (butler, "struck on the face" rumor).

### Ch XII, The Unexpected Guest
- Evening at vicarage. Bardon gave crystallized pebble; he takes credit on "debts."
- Mrs. Aumerle plays chess with Bardon. Cecilia sings "Bel raggio lusinghier."
- Mabel asks to go up in balloon with Augustine. Mrs. Aumerle: "That's pride." Augustine invites Bardon and Cecilia to ascent. Bardon refuses to meet earl.
- Red liveried carriage arrives; Annabella enters haggard. Vicar's wife Barbara; Ida takes Annabella's room.
- Bardon: Dashleigh is "my enemy."

### Ch XIII, The Friend's Mission
- Mrs. Aumerle lectures Mabel: wife should submit. Mabel: "Papa could never but welcome..."
- Narrator: Mabel's pride vs Ida's influence.
- Augustine goes to earl; earl's terms: Annabella must ask forgiveness and return that day.
- Annabella rejects ("I will not go and beg pardon"). Vicar sends for Bardon.

### Ch XIV, A Fatal Step
- Bardon hears Annabella's story. False rumour (Papists, mass, prayer to Virgin). Bardon urges republishing "Precipice" in magazine: "It would be revenge!"
- Ida knocks; Annabella: "I can't be disturbed." Augustine's carriage ready; Augustine says "Farewell, Mrs. Aumerle."
- Annabella seals two envelopes: "Precipice" to magazine editor; "Fairy Lake" to London publisher, under title "Countess of Dashleigh."
- Ring given at wedding recalled. Annabella calls Bates back too late; Mabel offers to fetch Bates; Annabella says no.

### Ch XV, The Deserted Home
- Earl misses wife. Pride forbids reconciling first. Reads magazine ad "THE FAIRY LAKE, by the Countess of Dashleigh." Reads article.
- Vicar's letter to earl (asks forgiveness, defends niece's shelter).
- Earl writes Augustine: reserve a place in balloon, 12th. Pride drives him.

### Ch XVI, Pleading
- Annabella: "I have broken my chain" (earlier) / confesses to Ida; "I cannot play the part of a penitent child."
- Ida: pride is of the world. Annabella: "You know not how wretched you make me."
- Mrs. Aumerle rebukes Annabella and Ida ("Rise, Ida"). Annabella resolves to leave for Dr. Bardon's cottage.
- Ida: "it was your coming that changed all!"

### Ch XVII, Conscience Asleep
- Bardon's religion does not change temper; "a good hater"; "forgive us... as we forgive."
- Bardon walks six miles to Pelton, library, no *Magazine* left. Librarian says piece "a hit on one of the leading men."

### Ch XVIII, The Magazine
- Bardon reads at Mrs. Clayton's (blind major's widow). Her cochlico lozenges; green tea.
- Bardon sees in Times: death of Mr. Auger of Nettleby Tower; gloats, "six feet of earth."
- Annabella arrives at Mill Cottage with Bates. Cecilia stitches drugget; Bardon welcomes her.
- Cecilia: "not a particle of pride."

### Ch XIX, Expectation
- Rumour: earl to ascend in *Eaglet*. Annabella stops eating.
- Bardon elects to attend. Mabel persuades father; father says ask "your mother's opinion." Mrs. Aumerle forbids.
- Ida argues with Mabel; ascent on 12 May. Vicar's wife "put an extinguisher" on it.

### Ch XX, A Sunny Morn
- Mabel rises early; Augustine's gig, horse Black Prince.
- Aspendale Lodge; Verdon: small, sharp features, grey eyes.
- Crowd; Bardon arrives: "The wind... will bear you towards Mill Cottage."
- Earl arrives in chariot with red liveries; pale.

### Ch XXI, The Ascent
- Earl frightened; drinks wine; Augustine tries to stop him. Earl pushes into car.
- Earl shouts "Let go!"; men release ropes; *Eaglet* rises. Verdon: "Merciful Heaven! they are lost!"
- Bardon: "How shall I tell this to Annabella?"

### Ch XXII, In the Clouds
- Augustine tries valve rope; breaks. Cloud, mist. Paper test.
- Whirlwind; wine cork pops; earl throws himself out, Augustine wrestles him. Earl faints.

### Ch XXIII, Regrets
- Ida regrets not stopping Mabel. Vicar and Ida visit Annabella at cottage; Cecilia present.
- Bardon gallops back: "Lost! lost!" names Augustine, Mabel, earl.
- Annabella cries out; sees balloon; Bardon: "I feel for you." Annabella curses him: "never let me behold you again."

### Ch XXIV, Soaring Above Pride
- Earl's repentance; text Isaiah 2:17 ("loftiness of man shall be bowed down").
- Gas leaks; knife fails. Mabel writes apology letter to Mrs. Aumerle; drops it.
- Earl gives Annabella's pocket-book; Mabel drops it. Evening prayer: Litany; earl leads.

### Ch XXV, A Broken Chain
- Annabella grieves. Ida prays in Mabel's room; lilac, Bible.
- Mrs. Aumerle comforts Lawrence. Ida confesses to stepmother. Mrs. Aumerle embraces Ida: "I believe there were faults on both sides."
- Pride flees: chain broken.

### Ch XXVI, The Awful Crisis
- Augustine's meditation; dawn; balloon less inflated.
- Ballast, instruments, basket thrown. Descends over the Channel.
- Augustine cuts cords; car falls on sea; Dashleigh's pocketbook and Mabel's hat for baling.
- Sea-gull false sail; then real sail; rescue.

### Ch XXVII, Tidings
- Night of waiting. Annabella's publisher note cancelling *Fairy Lake*.
- Telegram from Cliff Cottage, B——, Devon: "Safe, thank God! ... brain fever ... A. A."
- Vicar and Annabella travel; Ida stays home; Mrs. Aumerle's soliloquy. Mabel's letter found by farmer; Mrs. Aumerle softens.

### Ch XXVIII, The Wheel Turns
- Bardon gets Nettleby Tower under Auger's will (sum equal to lawsuit costs). Cecilia rejoices, Bardon sullen.
- Night journey; station official; Dr. G—— at Cliff Cottage; chaise; fisherman's shingle cottage on the shore; Mabel in father's arms.

### Ch XXIX, Two Words
- Dr. G—— forbids Annabella entry. Night on floor of fisherman's hut.
- Augustine and Lawrence on shore: Augustine's faith confessed.
- Annabella finds pocket-book with two pencilled words: "forgiveness" and "peace." Earl's forgiveness.

### Ch XXX, The Spirit Laid
- July. Earl convalescent; Annabella submissive; reads *The Fairy Lake*.
- Earl proposes visit to Bardon at Nettleby Tower. Visit: Cecilia, Aumerles, Ida, Mabel, Augustine present.
- Bardon's pride tested at "Dashleigh" name. Earl offers hand; Bardon grasps; enmity ends.
- Author's coda: Pride's forms; poem; "cut the cords of your balloon."

## BOOK 2: *The Boy Traders; or, The Sportsman's Club Among the Boers* (Harry Castlemon; Gutenberg 56868)

### Ch I, The Sandwich Islands
- Schooner *Stranger*, captain Uncle Dick (Gaylord), nephews Walter and Eugene. Frank Nelson sailing-master. Sailing quiz on cyclones in southern hemisphere.
- Recap: Honolulu; *Tycoon*; Captain Barclay; Walter captured by robbers (Potter's ranche); Archie lassoed wild horse; Zack and Silas; Pike's quartz mill.
- Hilo surfboard swimming; Archie vs Eugene; native Mr. Kanaker.
- Volcano of Kilauea. Trappers Dick Lewis and Bob Kelly terrified. They decide to go with Uncle Dick.

### Ch II, The Gale
- Mangrove Islands. Thirty-pounder *Long Tom* fires; natives flee. Anchor off former *Tycoon* anchorage.
- Storm. Dick Lewis: "Is that ole whale comin'?" Rodgers. Cabin battened. Storm damage: flying jibboom, topmasts gone, bulwarks smashed.

### Ch III, The Last of Long Tom
- Cyclone: Mr. Baldwin (first mate) explains. Uncle Dick turns off. Chase's letter about storm.
- Ship *Sea Gull* in trouble; crew of *Stranger* pump. *Long Tom* thrown overboard.
- Gets through reef. Natives in canoes; shrapnel shot kills about 300 (Uncle Dick: "at least three hundred").

### Ch IV, A Change of Programme
- *Sea Gull* wrecked on reef; boats rescue eleven. Second mate's boat.
- Frank stands night watch; Waters (giant convict) and three others suspected escaped convicts from Van Diemen's Land. Plan: go to Hobart Town.
- Archie: "We want a change."

### Ch V, The Two Champions
- Waters insolent to Mr. Parker (second mate). Boatswain's mate Lucas. Waters punches Lucas.
- Waters seizes handspike; Dick Lewis subdues him. Master-at-arms irons him.
- Waters' three friends given warning. Archie vs Eugene race talk. Dick's race idea.

### Ch VI, The Consul's "Clark"
- Hobart Town. Fowler, consul's clerk, arrives; patronising; "Hinglish." Police commissioner boat.
- Waters identified; Fowler's gold eyeglass. Uncle Dick's bribe story (Bendigo mines, ounce of gold, man-hunter).
- Dinner; Archie's Rocky Mountain jokes.

### Ch VII, More About the Clerk
- Sheep station of Mr. Wilbur (Gus Fowler is his friend). Dick beats Eugene's horse in race.
- Australia trip; Archie's horse stolen by bushrangers.
- Hobart Town again. Fowler asks Frank about the strong box, safe, and sailing.
- Fowler sends sailors on fake race; locks Frank in cabin. Schooner taken by convicts.

### Ch VIII, On the Quarter-deck Again
- Waters, Bob (ticket-of-leave man with revolver), Fowler, three crewmen. Archie posed as Walter. Plan: Walter's safe; bills of credit.
- Convict history: escapes, Sea Gull shipping. Bob ticket-of-leave, Fowler knew sailing schedules.
- Frank forced to command.

### Ch IX, A Yankee Trick
- Fowler lures Walter; Walter refuses. Bob captures Archie by mistake (in Walter's black suit and Panama hat).
- Frank pretends schooner is "smuggler," hides lights, slips past steamer. Waters praises "Yankee trick."
- Archie: "I wasn't born" (to fight in 1812 joke).

### Ch X, Archie Proves Himself a Hero
- Archie irons sleeping Waters (keeps tarpaulin on skylights). Takes two revolvers.
- Recaptures schooner with Brown and Stevens and negro cook "the Doctor." Fowler ironed.
- Waters offers "the Doctor" a thousand pounds; refused.
- British steamer: flag shown; lieutenant (gray-headed) boards; Frank refuses to yield.

### Ch XI, An Obstinate Captain
- Midshipman Kendall insolent; flag hauled down, then up again. Lieutenant returns; tug with Uncle Dick, Mr. Wilbur, Club.
- Uncle Dick discharges three crew who had joined convicts. Voyage to Natal.

### Ch XII, Buying an Outfit
- Natal; English colonel's outfit at Grahamstown. Scotch transport-rider McGregor ("Mack").
- Outfit: span of oxen, wagon (18 ft), six salted horses, double-barrel rifles. Lottery for horses/guns: Frank draws #3 (vicious horse "crowbait" and heavy elephant gun "killdeer"); Archie gets thoroughbred and silver-mounted rifle (Maynard).
- Kaffir servants; thief letter. Trek begins.

### Ch XIII, A Surly Boer
- Mynheer Schrader, field cornet, refuses trade. Frank repairs Griqua gun for "Mr. Jones."
- Mack: Boers, Griquas, Zulus. Lion veldt warning. Eugene dares Archie and Fred to night in shooting-hole.

### Ch XIV, A Troop of Lions
- Fountain; shooting-hole. Jackal yelping. Archie, Fred, Eugene shoot at "lions."
- Uncle Dick and Frank arrive with firebrands.

### Ch XV, "Where's My Horse?"
- Creature is a wild dog pack, not lions. Mack says Bushmen threat; Kaffirs grumble.
- Archie's horse stays in woods; returns. Mack suspiciously anxious.
- Walter and Bob on guard. Mack "takes Walter's horse and gun" to catch a Kaffir.

### Ch XVI, Deserted
- Mack gone (Walter's horse and gun). Kaffirs desert with oxen, horses, Uncle Dick's double-barrel.
- Walter as driver; whip hits his ear.
- Griqua village; Zulu delegation demands rifle; chief rages; Dick Lewis's war dance drives them off ("medicine-man").

### Ch XVII, Conclusion
- Griqua guides desert; oxen trail back.
- Zulu ambush in dry stream-bed; chief shot by Bob. Spear kills Archie's horse; Archie's leg pinned.
- Frank saves Archie; spear stopped by Frank's cartridge haversack.
- Boers trade cattle; Mack sold horse and gun in Grahamstown and fled.
- Homecoming to Bellville; Gaylord plantation; cannon salute.
- Epilogue: Frank a lawyer; Archie civil engineer, married; Chase & Wilson, Florida orange plantation; Fred Craven, revenue service lieutenant; Jasper Babcock, cotton factor; George Le Dell, Memphis; Phil Perkins, steamers; Walter and Eugene run plantation; Uncle Dick's cabin.
